paragraphs.text: 1. I AM prepared to laud with song or worship the Noble Ones who are in earth and heaven,
paragraphs.original: वसूनां वा चर्कृष इयक्षन्धिया वा यज्ञैर्वा रोदस्योः ।
paragraphs.translit: vasūnāṃ vā carkṛṣa iyakṣandhiyā vā yajñairvā rodasyoḥ |

paragraphs.text: Or Coursers who have triumphed in, the contest, or those who famed, have won the prize with glory.
paragraphs.original: अर्वन्तो वा ये रयिमन्तः सातौ वनुं वा ये सुश्रुणं सुश्रुतो धुः
paragraphs.translit: arvanto vā ye rayimantaḥ sātau vanuṃ vā ye suśruṇaṃ suśruto dhuḥ

paragraphs.text: 2. Their call, the call of Gods, went up to heaven: they kissed the ground with glory-seeking spirit,
paragraphs.original: हव एषामसुरो नक्षत द्यां श्रवस्यता मनसा निंसत क्षाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: hava eṣāmasuro nakṣata dyāṃ śravasyatā manasā niṃsata kṣām |

paragraphs.text: There where the Gods look on for happy fortune, and like the kindly heavens bestow their bounties.
paragraphs.original: चक्षाणा यत्र सुविताय देवा द्यौर्न वारेभिः कृणवन्त स्वैः
paragraphs.translit: cakṣāṇā yatra suvitāya devā dyaurna vārebhiḥ kṛṇavanta svaiḥ

paragraphs.text: 3. This is the song of those Immortal Beings who long for treasures in their full perfection.
paragraphs.original: इयमेषाममृतानां गीः सर्वताता ये कृपणन्त रत्नम् ।
paragraphs.translit: iyameṣāmamṛtānāṃ gīḥ sarvatātā ye kṛpaṇanta ratnam |

paragraphs.text: May these, completing prayers and sacrifices, bestow upon us wealth where naught is wanting.
paragraphs.original: धियं च यज्ञं च साधन्तस्ते नो धान्तु वसव्यमसामि
paragraphs.translit: dhiyaṃ ca yajñaṃ ca sādhantaste no dhāntu vasavyamasāmi

paragraphs.text: 4. Those living men extolled thy deed, O Indra, those who would fain burst through the stall of cattle,
paragraphs.original: आ तत्त इन्द्रायवः पनन्ताभि य ऊर्वं गोमन्तं तितृत्सान् ।
paragraphs.translit: ā tatta indrāyavaḥ panantābhi ya ūrvaṃ gomantaṃ titṛtsān |

paragraphs.text: Fain to milk her who bare but once, great, lofty, whose Sons are many and her streams past number.
paragraphs.original: सकृत्स्वं ये पुरुपुत्रां महीं सहस्रधारां बृहतीं दुदुक्षन्
paragraphs.translit: sakṛtsvaṃ ye puruputrāṃ mahīṃ sahasradhārāṃ bṛhatīṃ dudukṣan

paragraphs.text: 5. Sacivan, win to your assistance Indra who never bends, who overcomes his foemen.
Rbhuksan, Maghavan, the hymn's upholder, who, rich in food, bears man's kind friend, the thunder.
paragraphs.original: ऋभुक्षणं मघवानं सुवृक्तिं भर्ता यो वज्रं नर्यं पुरुक्षुः
paragraphs.translit: ṛbhukṣaṇaṃ maghavānaṃ suvṛktiṃ bhartā yo vajraṃ naryaṃ purukṣuḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. Since he who won of old anew hath triumphed, Indra hath earned his name of Vrtra-slayer.
He hath appeared, the mighty Lord of Conquest. What we would have him do let him accomplish.
